statement: The overlay provider's decisions — anchor resolution against a real scene, placement and clipping avoidance, motion intent under reduced motion, the input-to-outcome lifecycle, and focus containment — are exercised as pure logic.

results.case: a node's centre maps through the camera into viewport space
changing the camera moves the anchor, so it must be recomputed
an identity present in the scene resolves to a point
an absent identity falls back to a labelled viewport transition
the fallback still carries the semantic identity
with no scene loaded the anchor is unavailable, not an error
an anchor naming a different scene does not resolve against this one
an anchor with room below places below it
an anchor near the bottom flips above rather than overflowing
a corner anchor still yields a box inside the viewport
no anchor point centres the overlay
an overlay larger than the viewport is reported, not drawn negative
the transform origin sits inside the overlay box
the declared intent is used when motion is not reduced
reduced motion substitutes the declared fallback
a dialog starts closed with no run and no result
opening expands from the anchor and focuses the first control
editing records the draft
an invalid submission submits nothing and keeps the dialog open
an invalid submission preserves the draft and focuses the first invalid
cancelling before submit invokes nothing
a valid submission moves to submitting and counts one invocation
a second submit while in flight is refused, not queued
a submitted request cannot be cancelled from the dialog
admission associates the run and collapses toward the input node
execution events apply while the run proceeds
an intermediate outcome updates its node without stealing focus
another run's terminal outcome shows an indicator, not a dialog
the active terminal outcome expands from the outcome anchor
dismissing collapses, restores focus and keeps the result indicator
dismissal does not erase the retained outcome
a retained result can be reopened from its node
a run that finishes immediately sequences without inventing delay
an immediate outcome is retained like any other
a refusal preserves the draft and shows why
acknowledging a refusal returns to editing without resubmitting
an uncertain delivery is retained for reconciliation
an uncertain delivery does not resubmit
changing input clears the displayed result but keeps the indicator
an outcome with no admitted run is refused
dismissing when nothing is open is refused
an unknown event is refused, not ignored
opening focuses the first suitable control
an explicit autofocus wins over document order
a disabled first control is skipped

Tab moves forward
Tab wraps from the last control to the first
Shift+Tab wraps from the first control to the last
a single focusable control wraps to itself rather than escaping
focus arriving from outside the trap is pulled to an end
with nothing focusable, containment still returns the dialog
after an invalid submission focus goes to the first invalid control

notEstablished: No browser or DOM implementation is available here, so nothing below the decision layer is executed: whether focus actually moved, whether an animation actually ran, and whether the overlay was actually painted are all unverified.
The provider's DOM layer in runtime/overlay-provider.js is unexercised.
Anchor recomputation is proven to depend on camera state; it has not been observed reacting to a real zoom, pan or resize.
No capability was invoked, and no dialog has been opened by a person.
